story.head: Trench warfare
paras: The Oilers won the teams’ first meeting this season, 4-1 in New York on Nov 1. The Oilers (12-3-3) beat Vancouver 4-2 on Saturday, and the Rangers have won three straight. Going in, the Rangers are third in the Metropolitan (tied for 12th in the NHL) and the Oilers first in the Pacific (tied for third).

The Rangers’ record (.583) is about what their chances are worth. The Oilers’ record (.750) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.595), largely thanks to their finishing. If the Oilers’ record were closer to their chances, like the Rangers’, these teams would be much closer in the standings, so don’t be surprised if this one is closer than the records suggest.

The Oilers (lowest) and the Rangers (2nd lowest) both lean hard on their top players. The Rangers forecheck as hard as almost anyone (2nd) and get a lot of their shots blocked (32nd). The Oilers ice the puck less than almost anyone (2nd) and have a dangerous power play (2nd). Edmonton has scored 4.11 goals a game, the most in the league. Both teams play slow, low-event hockey, so expect a tight one. Beyond that, both teams like to hit, so expect plenty of it.

Adam Fox (2 G / 20 A / 22 P in 18 GP) leads the Rangers in scoring, and Alexis Lafrenière (9 G / 9 A / 18 P in 18 GP) has a team-high nine goals. Connor McDavid (10 G / 37 A / 47 P in 18 GP) leads the Oilers and the whole NHL in scoring, with eleven points in his last five games and four goals in six games against the Rangers since 2023-24. Leon Draisaitl (16 G / 18 A / 34 P in 18 GP) has a team-high 16 goals, tied for the most in the NHL, with ten points in his last five games.
Dylan Garand (6-6-1 / .906 SV% in 11 GS) is expected to start for the Rangers, and Devon Levi (7-1-0 / .888 SV% in 8 GS) for Edmonton.
At home, Mike Babcock likes to send Jones, Michaels and Frederic out against opponents’ fourth lines, so watch for them against Chmelař, Laba and Rempe.
